systemic_fix: One change, and it is the same one the data has now pointed at three weeks running — but this week it is unanimous: follow_through scored 3/3 on all nineteen accounts and ownership is right behind it at 2.84. Give every account ONE named owner who posts a short written update every Friday containing a number, what shipped, and every open promise marked done or dated. Nineteen of nineteen analyst top-fixes describe some version of this. Pair it with a hard rule: no new ask goes to a client who has an unanswered request older than 48 hours.
team_broadcast: Team — three changes, effective today. 1) Every client now has ONE named owner (list out this afternoon). Owners: nothing sits unanswered past 24 hours, even if the honest answer is 'I don't know yet, I'll come back to you Thursday'. If you see a question for someone else's client, tag the owner. 2) Every Friday, each owner posts a short written update in their client's chat: a number, what shipped this week, and every open item with a date next to it. Clients who can't see the work assume there isn't any — that is exactly how we lost Paige and Chey Mai, and both of them paid us on time until the day they left. 3) Two hard stops: credentials never go in a group chat again — not requested, not posted, and anything currently sitting in a chat gets rotated this week; and no client gets a new content demand or a work-pause warning while we owe them an answer older than 48 hours. Several of the pause-work lines that went out on September 1 went to clients whose only blocker was us. That stops now.
pattern: We are applying pressure to the people who pay us and silence to the people who ask us questions. Every account we are currently losing — Barbara, Haileigh, Kaitlynn, Amber Haze, Vale, Mila — pays on time, and every one of them got a quota, a broadcast, or a work-pause threat during the same window in which their actual question went unanswered. Meanwhile the four things clients praised this week were all the same shape: someone explained something honestly, in writing, before being chased. That is the entire difference between the saves and the losses.
